2026-09-02T12:40:00.7549751Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7550818Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7573582Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7575027Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7576023Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7576951Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7579269Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7583915Z >
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7586453Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7589052Z >
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7589915Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7590740Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7590942Z ### How to Use
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7591485Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7592611Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7594203Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7594428Z ```bash
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7595128Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7596531Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7597246Z ```
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7597985Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7598322Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7598921Z ```bash
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7600049Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7602773Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7604386Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7605940Z ```
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7606183Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7606961Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7607925Z ```bash
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7608547Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7609294Z ```
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7609524Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7609879Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7610831Z ```bash
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7611687Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7613399Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7614211Z ```
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7614440Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7614988Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7615476Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7617174Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7619686Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7619895Z ```bash
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7620404Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7621575Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7622478Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7622835Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7623409Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7624494Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7625385Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7625913Z ```
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7626138Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7626939Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7627938Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7628134Z ```bash
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7628891Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7629881Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7630665Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7631369Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7631878Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7632784Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7633390Z ```
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7633622Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7633864Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7635670Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7637348Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7638572Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7640216Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7642269Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7643956Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7644188Z ### Notes
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7646139Z 
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7646902Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7648470Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7650263Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7667100Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7670638Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7673031Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7675877Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-02T12:40:00.7676721Z </mcp-clis>
